name: 18 Wheeler
label: Creation Records
lede: Oasis got signed on 18 Wheeler's bill at King Tut's. 18 Wheeler went on to make three albums for the same label, the last with a Sex Pistol on bass.

eras.title: The night someone else got signed
eras.text: A Glasgow guitar-pop band with a record out on August Records, 18 Wheeler were on the bill at King Tut's on the night Alan McGee first saw Oasis. McGee's label, Creation Records, put out their albums for the next four years.

years.cap: Oasis backstage at King Tut's Wah Wah Hut, Glasgow, on 18 Wheeler's bill, May 31, 1993
years.src: Wikipedia: 18 Wheeler · Radio X · The New Vinyl Villain
years.h: Oasis talk their way onto 18 Wheeler's bill at King Tut's
years.p: The advertised bands are Glasgow's Boyfriend and 18 Wheeler and Manchester's Sister Lovers. Oasis, not on the bill, get four songs, and McGee signs them.
years.xp: Wikipedia and the New Vinyl Villain both have 18 Wheeler headlining and Oasis as the unknown support. McGee had come to surprise Debbie Ellis of Sister Lovers, an old friend, Radio X reports; he ended up offering Oasis a deal.

years.src: Discogs: Nature Girl · Creation Records: Interview
years.h: The 'Nature Girl' 12-inch, with David Keenan still on guitar
years.p: Out on August Records with 'Pillow Fight' and the six-minute 'Golden Candles' on the flip. [[Sean Jackson|96349407-a671-4382-985a-5f80301af696]], [[David Keenan|587ca259-c2fc-41ba-b64b-7704b92488bf]], [[Alan Hake|9932aa39-d177-4cc3-8530-3e6fb9161289]] and [[Neil Halliday|11473f21-3672-4dd8-bbbf-1b5fe9520806]] are the band.
years.xp:
The route in ran through Teenage Fanclub. Jackson says Norman Blake heard their demo and told them to send it to Dave Barker, then running Paperhouse. Barker was moving to Creation to set up a subsidiary, August, and wanted 18 Wheeler on it.

When August wound down, the band moved over to Creation proper.

eras.title: Three albums on Creation
eras.text: Craig Leon produced the first album, Creation co-founder Joe Foster the next two, and by the third there were samples and a Sex Pistol on bass. Creation let them go in the middle of the fourth.

years.h: David Keenan leaves to start the Telstar Ponies
years.p: Keenan forms the Telstar Ponies, later on Fire Records. [[Steven Haddow|41fbcc45-29a6-4d63-82d2-087e327844c3]] takes over on guitar.

years.h: Twin Action, produced by Craig Leon at Britannia Row
years.p: Fourteen songs on Creation, recorded in London and Aberdeen with Craig Leon and co-producer Paul Fyfe. 'Kum Back' and 'The Revealer' go out as singles.
years.xp: Strings, pedal steel and Mellotron fill out the trio of Jackson, Hake and Halliday on the sleeve credits; Idha Ovelius sings a duet. Anjali Dutt mixed it.

years.h: Formanka comes with a second disc of home demos
years.p: Ten songs produced by Creation co-founder [[Joe Foster|6a850a84-6293-4788-9e05-ccd9fd4f0315]]. The limited edition adds four home demos, including earlier singles 'Kum Back' and 'The Revealer'.

years.h: Alan Hake trains his Oasis binoculars on Kate Moss at Knebworth
years.p: Everyone backstage got Oasis-branded binoculars. Hake pointed his at the roped-off VIP platform, "much to Kate Moss's displeasure," Jackson recalled.

years.h: Tony Blair introduces 18 Wheeler at the Labour Party Conference
years.p: Blair, then Labour leader, does the introduction at the 1996 conference. Asked about it in 2010, Jackson said: "We all do stupid things when we are young."

years.src: Discogs: Year Zero · Wikipedia: 18 Wheeler · Bigwig
years.h: Glen Matlock plays bass on Year Zero
years.p: A sample-based turn, co-produced with Foster, with the [[Sex Pistols|e5db18cb-4b1f-496d-a308-548b611090d3]]' Glen Matlock on bass and strings arranged by [[Terry Edwards|4f9f3ee1-e2cf-4d6a-8e5c-9412b42a3bad]].
years.xp:
Remixed, 'Stay' gets radio play and reaches No. 59 in March: the band's only UK Top 75 single. 'The Hours and the Times' and 'Grease' were also singles.

In October 1996 Bigwig found them in a soundproofed room near London Bridge, building songs from an eight-track guitar part up. Jackson put the new sound down to "listening to a lot more dance music."

years.h: Creation drops the band during the fourth album
years.p: The label lets 18 Wheeler go with the album nearly done. Hake keeps the master tapes, and no official release has followed.
years.xp:
"Sony's accountants were in no mood for more Wheeler," Jackson said in 2010 (Sony owned 49% of Creation). He thought the label might as well have released it, since it was already paid for.

Their manager later passed Creation a work tape of the album. Jackson heard it was being played in the office, and their old A&R man told him they thought it was "fucking brilliant".

eras.title: Slots, Must Destroy
eras.text: After the band, Jackson spent years in Central and Eastern Europe and Hake went into running a label.

years.h: Sean Jackson's Slots arrives five years after he cut it
years.p: Recorded in 2005, his folk-leaning solo album appears on PoppyDisc Records. Alan Hake, meanwhile, co-founds the Must Destroy label.
years.xp:
Iestyn Polson offered to produce it for free at his home studio, Jackson said, and Joe Foster put it out on PoppyDisc. Hake, by then, was also running 45cat, a website for his love of vinyl singles.

Looking back on the band, Jackson counted "4 albums, about 15 eps" in five years, plus the Albert Hall UnDrugged night, tours with Teenage Fanclub and Sebadoh, and "a mild outbreak of Wheelermania in Japan."

years.p: His daughter shared the news, according to Wikipedia. Wikipedia gives no cause.
